As fun as Borderlands is, I feel that the Borderlands series personally had a few small issues. The navigation is fun at first, but sometimes can drag and become the worst part. The Pre-Sequel especially, which was a very fun game that was kind of plagued with a few navigation issues, and a lot of annoying back and forth.

Borderlands 2 does improve on the navigation, a little. However, I ran into several issues during my first returning playthrough that rubbed me the wrong way. Namely, which, Borderlands 2's PhysX implementation on PC, which is infamous to make loot disappear and cause many problems if on anything higher than Low.

And there were a little more than 'loot disappearing'. When this was set to high, it prevented the game from working past loading my save, at all. Setting it to 'Low' did fix the problem, however why this is even a problem is ridiculous.

I also ran into issues with the game difficulty being a bit high for my taste (I found myself going down a little more than I felt I should), as well as this being tenfold more apparent by minibosses I killed seemignly not remaining dead. Because lo and behold, I loaded my save after playing last night, struggled with the PhysX issue, then struggled with enemies being magically alive after having killed them the last time I was on.

Borderlands 2 is a fun game, however the issues it's plagued with made me not want to play anymore. And it's a shame, because Borderlands 2 is an amazing sequel to the original, and improves the original game in many ways.

citations.review_text: Game is fine if played solo but if you're trying to play co-op, there's a chance it won't work. Many forum posts out there from other people having the exact same issue my friends and I are having. Spent hours trying to find a solution. Just trying to stay connected to the main lobby with other people has problems (getting kicked, Not being available to join or not being able to join via invite). I don't know a fix, and after reading various forums and boards, There's really seems to be no solution to fix it.

Literally impossible to play with friends for more than 10-15 minutes before something happens (loss of connection, getting kicked, the game soft locks) and it takes a series of restarting the game and/or your computer to even attempt to rejoin the other player. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as padded with excessive backtracking and travel across large areas that take too long to cross.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Borderlands 2[/h1]
[b]Rating:[/b] 6/10  A Good Game That Doesn't Quite Match the Memory

[h1]The Short Version[/h1]
[b]Verdict:[/b] Borderlands 2 is a real step up from the first game in most ways that matter, guns feel better, abilities are more fun, loot is more satisfying. But replaying the main campaign now, it doesn't hold up as well as I remembered. Missions feel thin, the areas are just okay, and the whole thing wraps up shorter than I expected.

[table]
[tr][th]Category[/th][th]Verdict[/th][/tr]
[tr][td]Main Campaign[/td][td]Padded With Travel[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]Gunplay & Abilities[/td][td]Big Step Up From BL1[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]Movement & Stability[/td][td]Slow, Some Bugs[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]DLC Content[/td][td]All Over the Place[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr][/hr]

[h1]Pandora, Revisited[/h1]
[i]"Still a good game. Just not the one I remembered."[/i]
Going back into the main campaign years later changed how I saw a lot of it. It's not bad, but my biggest issue is how much travel it forces on you, sending you back and forth across areas that take forever to cross for no real reason other than to pad out playtime. The missions themselves rarely rise above fine, and the areas blend together after a while. By the end, the campaign felt shorter than it should have.
[list]
[*] [b]Missions:[/b] Nothing outright bad here, just not much that stuck with me.
[*] [b]Travel:[/b] A lot of forced back-and-forth across areas that take too long to cross, feels like padding more than anything else.
[*] [b]Pacing:[/b] It wrapped up sooner than I expected.
[/list]

[h1]The Guns Talk Louder Than the Story[/h1]
[i]"Everything about the shooting got better. Everything else is a mixed bag."[/i]
This is where Borderlands 2 earns its reputation. The guns feel much better than in the first game, and the abilities stayed fun to use the whole way through. It's a real leap forward from the original. Loot felt good to chase too. Most of my complaints here are about pacing and polish, not the c…

What can I say except "wow!"

Playing this game 14 years after release and it still holds up incredibly well. This is one of few games that I just couldn't put down. Every day was more progress and more deep learning into the lore and background of the Borderlands world. The world is super varied with its characters, monsters, biomes and core focuses (especially when you consider the DLCs). There's also great variety with the artstyle, weapons, etc.

Everyone I met was unique and fascinating to learn about. These days, most game characters embody a specific stereotype/trope. In Borderlands 2, each of the characters feel deeper than that. At first they hit a stereotype, but then they each have deeper story arcs and personalities.

There are a couple of minor gripes I'd like to mention. The biggest of which is "Why does 'Save and Quit' take you to the closest Fast Travel???". That fast travel sometimes being 45 minutes of progress away (especially in the first 5 hours). There's also:

- A little bit of grinding required, but I'm fine with that given how fun the Side Missions are.
- Hard to tell which side missions are small, and which ones are multi-part stories.
- No "Restock All" buttons in stores (but I'm sure that's fixed on later entries).

Overall, a thoroughly enjoyable experience. It's almost perfect, and I cant wait to jump back in for the DLCs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring an extensive variety of weapons, builds, and character classes that provide high replay value and a rewarding loot grind.

citations.review_text:
An excellent looter shooter with a huge variety of weapons and builds. Trying different guns and finding better gear is incredibly satisfying, and the amount of content makes the grind feel rewarding rather than pointless. A fantastic game, especially in co-op.

100% Completion
Time : 154.9H
Completion Difficulty : 4/10
Playthroughs : 2 + character cleanup + additional progression is required for the endgame/ raid bosses
Missables : None
DLC Required : Yes
Notable requirements : Complete a large amount of campaign and DLC content, defeat the raid bosses.

Play this game. I have played so many playthroughs on pc and console and I have always felt that each and every run has felt different. The build diversity and weapon variations will keep you coming back playthrough after playthrough. The storytelling is phenomenal and the world building continued to become a complete masterpiece after the setup from Borderlands 1. The main cast of playable characters are all unique with their builds and roles and they feel completely different from the other. With the randomization of the weapons, it leaves you wanting to find more that suit your needs alongside farming for guaranteed weapon drops from bosses or common/uncommon enemies. Each and every element, if applicable on that weapon, have a usage and will never feel like you've wasted your time. The main story is one of the best written stories I have played. Each mission will suck you into this world they created and the pacing is phenomenal. The side quests are worth it and it would be a shame if you were to skip them. Major props to all of the voice actors and the dialogue written for them, and there wasn't any wasted potential anywhere in sight. I will fight tooth and nail about the main antagonist, Handsome Jack, being one of the most well-written video game villains of all time. As I have played through the other games in the franchise, no other villain has been able to top what he has been able to fulfill for the player's enjoyment. I have played through the entire game across the years and I still haven't felt bored with each and every run. This game made me experience every emotion possible. While the main storyline is a masterpiece, the DLCs have a lot to offer. They are all written carefully, they don't overwrite the story and add new unique additions that will make you want to play through them again and again. I will continue playing this game as long as I can and I will never want to leave the world of Pandora entirely. Again, please play this game.

Many things change, but Borderlands 2 being one of the shooters of all time will not. An addictive combat loop, combined with vast replayability with the six vault hunters creates a fun experience that improves on the first game in every way. Skill trees have gone from basic to incredibly complex, offering the opportunity for an infinite number of playstyles and combinations. Most weapons in the game are fun to use and getting a legendary has never felt as good as it does in this game. The story is surprisingly good, and Handsome Jack is one of the most recognizable and memorable villains in a video game. You add all things up, along with a plethora of extra content and you have a game that is easy to sink hundreds of hours into. You can get it on sale often, so pick a copy up. It's worth at least one (hundred) playthroughs.

Borderlands 2 is a blast from start to finish. The humor hits, the characters are unforgettable, and Handsome Jack remains one of the best villains in gaming. Gunplay feels fantastic, the loot loop is endlessly addictive, and every class brings a fresh, unique playstyle. Even years after release, it's still one of the best, and easily the peak of the Borderlands series, delivering nonstop action, charm, and replayability.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the multiplayer and online co-op systems suffer from severe connectivity issues, disconnection drops, and server problems when trying to play with friends.

citations.review_text: Fun game if you intended to only play by yourself for 1-2 playthroughs. Nearly impossible to play with friends in 2026 due to bugs, glitches, and the migration to the SHiFT servers. Would not recommend purchasing at this time to anyone looking to play multiplayer.

This used to be one of my favorite games to play with friends. It used to work incredibly well. My friends could appear in my games at random to annoy me, and it was all in good fun.

That is no longer the case. With the ToS updates (which are their own controversy) have seemingly come some new backend changes that make it almost impossible to play with my friend. I wanted to show him the good gameplay, and fun writing of this game, but instead, we found hardlocks.

Changing network settings to switch from offline mode to friends only? The game hardlocks.
Booting up the game and trying to load the title screen? 25% chance the game hardlocks.
Attempt to join your friend through steam? 50% chance the game hardlocks.
Connection times out while trying to join your friend? The game hardlocks.
Friend has a minor internet hiccup? You get kicked back to the title screen, and the game hardlocks.
Got kicked back to the title screen and restarted the game to escape the hardlock? Well, you have to go into network settings and turn it back to online, which, of course, hardlocks, but at least it remembers you changed it.

We have spent more time trying to make the game work than actually playing it.

Not to mention another friend I played the game with a few years ago. The game encountered a crash, and for some reason this led to the game permanently blocking us from joining each other ever again. We tried everything to fix this reinstalling, forums, changing settings, blocking and unblocking. We even called gearbox support, who was unable to fix the issue after several hours. I miss playing with them.

It's sad to see what this game has become. It used to be such a straightforward good time.

Unfortunately I really love this game and leaving it a bad review hurts. However an update that occurred a few weeks ago has completely ruined being able to play this game online in co-op. It will take 5-6 restarts to even get the game to connect to online servers and then a couple more restarts to be able to join my friends lobby. Then after 30min of getting into a lobby you have maybe 15min of stable play before you get disconnected and have to restart the process. This is incredibly frustrating and I am not hopeful that gearbox isnt using this to push players to BL4.

Fix your damn servers its impossible to play with a friend for more than 3 hrs consistantly. It doesnt matter who is hosting the wifi speed or anything one of us gets booted ALWAYS. Very frustrating. Fix your damn servers

One of the best games of all time, that I will never be able to play again with my friends because of greed and incompetence. The multiplayer system is completely gutted, broken, and glitched out. I don't know how its possible to screw something up so royally after it had been functioning for literal decades. It is with a heavy heart that I leave a negative review on this masterpiece, but we have to let them know when we get screwed. 

If you're not playing with friends, this is still one of the best single player campaigns ever. But wow, what a huge loss for gaming.

Still a great game to play. A lot of replay value with the amount of characters you can play as and the different guns you can get with different modifiers. However, because it is a old game that doesn't get any more maintenance updates, multiplayer experience has suffered immensely. If you are thinking of buying this with multiplayer in mind, be prepared to learn how to set up a virtual LAN to use LAN, otherwise you will suffer disconnection issues that make the game unplayable.
Fun game, Lots of loot. Wish Multiplayer worked tho.

I loved playing this game but it is currently completely unplayable. I have spent hours troubleshooting problems trying to play the game recently and have been unable to get online play working. The game just gets stuck on creating online session whenever I attempt to play online. Very disappointed since I loved the game when I played it a few years ago and am now unable to share it with others. The sentiment I found online seemed to be that a 2024 SHiFT integration update broke online play somewhat but I have no clue.
